ticket.summary: No hot water — gas water heater pilot lights then self-extinguishes after ~10 min (likely failed thermocouple); no gas odor, no leak; infant in home, needs first morning slot.
mitigation_advice: Confirmed no gas odor; instructed to leave home and call gas utility/911 from outside if gas smell ever occurs
Turn gas control knob to OFF instead of repeatedly relighting the pilot
Heat water on stove and mix to warm for the 4-month-old, test temperature on wrist before use
Confirmed no water pooling at base of tank — no active leak

quote_lines.description: After-hours-booked standard diagnostic, gas water heater
Thermocouple replacement, parts + labor (estimate, pending on-site diagnosis)

ticket.customer_message: That's a relief — no gas smell and no water on the floor means this isn't an emergency, so we don't need to page the on-call plumber tonight. A pilot that burns ~10 minutes and dies is the classic sign of a failing thermocouple. Tonight: turn the gas control to OFF rather than relighting repeatedly; heat water on the stove and mix to warm for the baby, testing on your wrist first; if you ever smell gas, call the gas utility or 911 from outside. I've put you in the first priority slot tomorrow, Tuesday Sept 1, 8:00–10:00 AM arrival (60–90 min on site). Pricing: thermocouple replacement typically $89 diagnostic + $145 parts/labor = $234 — but since we installed your heater last year this is very likely warranty-covered ($0 to you). The office will verify the warranty first thing and confirm before charging anything. Dispatch will text confirmation around 7:00 AM.
